nodes.label: Quickselect
nodes.rationale: Partitioning tells you which side the answer is on, so you recurse into ONE side: n + n/2 + n/4 + ... = 2n instead of n log n. The recursive call is in tail position, so write it as a loop and the space is Theta(1).

nodes.label: Partition Postcondition (Neither Side Is Sorted)
nodes.rationale: 'Partial sort' is a misleading label. select_nth_unstable guarantees a PARTITION — everything before k is <= v[k], everything after is >= it — and establishing order within the prefix is precisely the work it skips, which is why it is Theta(n). Passing &v[..k] to a binary search is silently wrong.

nodes.label: slice::select_nth_unstable
nodes.rationale: Introselect: starts with a fast pivot strategy and falls back to a guaranteed-Theta(n) method on poor splits, so the worst case is bounded regardless of input. Measured 1.21 ms vs 13.01 ms for a full sort on top-10 of 1M u64 (10.7x). It reorders the whole slice, so preserving the input costs a clone.

nodes.label: Median-of-Medians (BFPRT)
nodes.rationale: Groups of 5 guarantee a pivot between the 30th and 70th percentile, bounding the recursion — the proof that Theta(n) worst-case selection is possible. Its ~10-20x constant means nobody runs it directly; it is the fallback that makes introselect's guarantee real, the same relationship heapsort has with introsort.

nodes.label: Streaming Top-k via Size-k Min-Heap
nodes.rationale: When n is unknown you cannot partition at all, because partitioning requires the whole array. A min-heap of size k has its root as the k-th largest, so most elements are rejected after one comparison: Theta(n log k) time, Theta(k) space, near-Theta(n) in practice for k << n.

nodes.label: Never Average Percentiles
nodes.rationale: Percentiles are not linear so they do not average — the p99 of a union is not a function of the per-part p99s, and one skewed host can dominate the global tail while its own p99 looks unremarkable. Averaging systematically understates the true p99, so SLOs get made on a fiction. Merge sketches centrally instead.

nodes.label: Maintain a Structure, Don't Recompute a Statistic
nodes.rationale: Selection is one-shot over a static array and has no incremental form, because its whole speed comes from destructively partitioning the data it was given. Over m updates, re-selecting is Theta(n*m). Two heaps give a running median in Theta(log n); a Fenwick or order-statistic tree gives rank queries over a changing set.

nodes.label: Three-Way (Dutch Flag) Partition
nodes.rationale: All-equal input is the sneakiest quadratic trigger because a two-way partition puts every element on one side — so the fix is a PARTITIONING change, not a pivot change. Costs speed on data with no duplicates.
